title: SF3583 (2023-2024 Regular): State preemption of local units of government regulating firearms repealer

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Minnesota) (gun-policy Stage 5, Minnesota); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Minnesota text (Introduction, 2024-02-13; official copy, https://www.revisor.mn.gov/bills/93/2024/0/SF/3583/versions/0/)
provenance.note: Introduced version, as filed (2024-02-13); official copy from revisor.mn.gov. No passage vote recorded. Section 2 repeals the preemption statutes (471.633, 471.634, 624.714 subd. 23, 624.717, 624.7191 subd. 4); their text is in the bill's appendix and is not quoted. Section 1 strikes the 'Notwithstanding section 471.633' opening and the cross-reference to sections 471.633 and 471.634.

operative_text:
Section 1 (Minn. Stat. 471.635): A governmental subdivision may regulate by reasonable, nondiscriminatory, and nonarbitrary zoning ordinances, the location of businesses where firearms are sold by a firearms dealer. For the purposes of this section, a firearms dealer is a person who is federally licensed to sell firearms.
Section 2 (repealer): REPEALER. Minnesota Statutes 2022, sections 471.633; 471.634; 624.714, subdivision 23; 624.717; and 624.7191, subdivision 4, are repealed.
